questions.q:
Solve the equation 3x² + 4x − 5 = 0.
Show all your working and give your answers correct to 2 decimal places.
questions.tip: Write the full formula with your numbers in it before using the calculator: that line earns the method marks.

questions.q:
(a) Write 3x² + 12x − 1 in the form a(x + b)² + c. [3]
(b) Write down the minimum value of 3x² + 12x − 1. [1]
questions.tip: Take the 3 out of the x terms only, and remember to multiply the −4 by 3.

questions.q:
The sides of a right-angled triangle are x cm, (x + 7) cm and (x + 8) cm. The hypotenuse is (x + 8) cm.
(a) Show that x² − 2x − 15 = 0. [3]
(b) Solve x² − 2x − 15 = 0 and find the perimeter of the triangle. [3]
ms: (a) M1: expands correctly: x² + x² + 14x + 49 = x² + 16x + 64
(a) A1: simplifies to x² − 2x − 15 = 0 with no errors
(b) A1: x = 5 (x = −3 rejected as a length cannot be negative)
questions.model:
(a) Pythagoras: x² + (x + 7)² = (x + 8)²
x² + x² + 14x + 49 = x² + 16x + 64
2x² + 14x + 49 − x² − 16x − 64 = 0
x² − 2x − 15 = 0
(b) (x − 5)(x + 3) = 0, so x = 5 or x = −3.
A length cannot be negative, so x = 5.
Sides 5, 12 and 13 cm: perimeter = 30 cm.
questions.tip: Always state why you reject a solution, e.g. 'a length cannot be negative'.

questions.q:
Lucy cycles 60 km at an average speed of x km/h.
On the return journey her average speed is 5 km/h slower, and the journey takes 1 hour longer.
(a) Show that x² − 5x − 300 = 0. [4]
(b) Solve the equation and find the time taken for the return journey. [3]
ms: (a) A1: multiplies by x(x − 5) correctly: 60x − 60(x − 5) = x(x − 5), leading to x² − 5x − 300 = 0 with no errors
questions.model:
(a) Time out = 60/x hours, time back = 60/(x − 5) hours.
60/(x − 5) − 60/x = 1
Multiply by x(x − 5): 60x − 60(x − 5) = x(x − 5)
300 = x² − 5x
x² − 5x − 300 = 0
(b) (x − 20)(x + 15) = 0, so x = 20 (a speed cannot be negative).
Return speed = 15 km/h, time = 60 ÷ 15 = 4 hours.
questions.tip: Time = distance ÷ speed. The slower journey takes longer, so subtract the shorter time from the longer one.
